abstract: Predicting daily sleep and stress states from lifelogs is difficult when labels are scarce, observations are participant-dependent, and validation does not match the hidden test distribution. We present an anchor-constrained ensemble for seven binary targets in the 5th ETRI Human Understanding AI Paper Challenge. A stable sequence-based anchor is blended with a pre-existing multi-signal model carrying a small same-participant nearest-neighbor correction over four sensor families. On 450 labeled person-days from 10 participants, the complete lineage ensemble obtains a non-nested local mean log loss of 0.534000 and a DACON public score of 0.5960832519, improving the previous public anchor by 0.0053280490. An OOF ablation attributes only 0.000508 of the 0.004638 local gain to the similarity correction; no public ablation isolates its leaderboard effect. More aggressive models transferred poorly, and three later near-anchor probes did not improve the result. The contribution is therefore the conservative ensemble and its explicit attribution and risk audit, not evidence that feature similarity alone caused the public gain.
title: Anchor-Constrained Feature-Similarity Ensembling for Multimodal Lifelog State Prediction
